comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PRE-EMPTIVE REMEDIATION before the first review, applying two defect classes that cost d8ef five rounds. I read every AC by hand rather than trusting my own keyword heuristic, which reported this ticket clean.

FIXED 1 — AC6 was the [operator-attested] trap in disguise. It required 'the change description and the follow-up record BOTH state that this relocates mass'. A Gerrit commit message and a ticket comment are both OUTSIDE the repository, and the completion verifier reads repository files ONLY — it explicitly cannot read git history. My keyword scan missed it because the AC says 'change description', not 'comment'. Split along the repo boundary: the caveat must now appear IN the new module's docstring (in-repo, and the place a future reader sizing up config.py's growth curve will actually meet it), with the commit-message half tagged [operator-attested].

FIXED 2 — AC2 was about to become FALSE. It said a seam test must assert a headroom target for llm/config.py 'which has no such guard today'. That is true right now and stops being true the moment sibling d8ef lands, because the guard I just wrote in tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py covers config.py at the staged <= 800. Reworded: this ticket TIGHTENS that existing guard to the < 700 policy target, in the same change that creates the headroom, rather than adding a second one. This is the ordering rule the hardening epic already uses — the change that buys the headroom is the change that may assert it.

Neither would have been caught by the heuristic sweep; both came from reading the criteria as a reviewer would. Cheaper here than as review rounds three and four.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ROUND 1: BLOCK, one finding, ACCEPTED after verifying it in source.

THE FINDING: assert_gated hardcodes logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config") at config.py:230. Move the function to gate_context.py and that logger identity goes stale — the REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning would be attributed to a module that no longer contains the code.

VERIFIED, and the verification changes how it should be fixed rather than whether: `grep -rn '"rebar.llm.config"' src/ tests/` returns exactly ONE line — that call site. No test filters on the logger name, no other source reference, no caplog assertion. So nothing BREAKS; the defect is purely observability, and re-pointing the logger is safe rather than risky.

WHY IT STILL EARNS AN AC RATHER THAN AN INCIDENTAL EDIT: the warning it emits is security-relevant and the message itself calls the override 'audited'. An audited warning filed under the wrong module sends whoever greps the logs to a file that does not contain the code. That is worth an explicit criterion and a test, not a silent fix-up during a relocation.

SWEPT THE CLASS BEFORE RESUBMITTING, per the lesson d8ef taught over five rounds. Searched the entire moved range (config.py:51-152 and :190-269) for identity-bearing literals: getLogger, __name__, __module__, quoted 'rebar.' strings and ContextVar names. Four hits — the one hardcoded logger, plus the three ContextVar debug names (rebar_llm_code_root and siblings). The ContextVar names stay ACCURATE after the move because the code remains under rebar.llm, and they are repr/debug only, so they need no change. The class is therefore limited to the single logger, and the new AC covers it.

Two defect classes had already been fixed on this ticket PRE-EMPTIVELY, before the first review: an out-of-repo AC requiring evidence in a Gerrit commit message and a ticket comment, and an AC asserting config.py 'has no such guard today' that sibling d8ef was about to falsify. Those two did not appear in this review's findings, which suggests the pre-emptive pass was worth doing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
COORDINATION HAZARD between this ticket and sibling b5fe — recorded as a COMMENT rather than an AC edit because this ticket's plan review is currently IN FLIGHT and editing its material mid-review is what caused 9227's first sign to fail with stale-pin-drift. Fold it into the ACs only after the review lands, if the reviewer has not already raised it.

BOTH b300 AND b5fe TIGHTEN THE SAME ASSERTION. tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py (shipped by d8ef) currently reads:

    for path in (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _LLM_CONFIG):
        loc = _loc(path)
        assert loc < _HARD_CAP

One loop, one shared bound, two files. b300's AC tightens llm/config.py to < 700 and b5fe's AC tightens plan_review/workflow_ops.py to < 700. Because the bound is SHARED, tightening it for either file also tightens it for the other — and the other is still ~793 until its own extraction lands. So the first of the two to land would go RED on its sibling's file.

REQUIRED SEQUENCING: whichever of b300/b5fe lands FIRST must split that loop into PER-FILE bounds (e.g. an explicit (path, bound) table) and set only its own file to 700, leaving the sibling at the staged 800. The second ticket then changes exactly one number. This is cheap if anticipated and a confusing red CI if not — the failure would name the OTHER ticket's file, so whoever hits it would look in the wrong place.

Found by reading b5fe's criteria as a reviewer before submitting it, not by a gate. b5fe's copy of this note is already in its AC text.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED: Gerrit change 1157, commit on feat/llm-provider-seam.

MEASURED: config.py 793 -> 631 (169 lines of headroom where there were 7); new
src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py at 243 LOC, clearing the 100-line anti-fragmentation floor. That is
room for d23e's 10-16-line deprecation alias plus roughly fifteen more config knobs at the measured
10-13 lines each.

HELD-OUT TDD, and it held. I authored 8 tests, confirmed RED for the right reasons (module absent,
config 793 > 700, warning attributed to rebar.llm.config, shared-bound loop present), then physically
removed the 5 held-out tests from the implementer's tree and handed it only the 3 happy-path cases.
It passed ALL FIVE it never saw — including the two that matter most: the re-export contract and the
no-repoint guard.

MUTATIONS, each restored afterwards:
  * repoint a REAL consumer (attest.py) at gate_context      -> 1 test fails
  * make gate_context import config at module scope (cycle)  -> 4 tests fail
  * revert the logger to the hardcoded "rebar.llm.config"    -> 1 test fails

THE FIRST MUTATION IS THE WHOLE POINT and is worth spelling out, because the failure mode is silent
rather than loud. Thirteen monkeypatch targets in the suite name `rebar.llm.config.<moved name>`.
They work because every consumer does a FUNCTION-LEVEL `from rebar.llm.config import ...`, resolving
out of config's globals at call time — exactly what setattr rebinds. Repoint one consumer to
gate_context and the patch still applies to config while the consumer reads elsewhere: THE PATCH
STOPS TAKING EFFECT AND ITS TEST KEEPS PASSING, asserting nothing. Nothing crashes; coverage silently
evaporates. That is why this ships both a structural guard (no src module may import from
gate_context) and a behavioural one (a patch on config must still reach a real consumer) rather than
trusting the relocation.

COORDINATION HAZARD RESOLVED IN THIS CHANGE. The d8ef seam test asserted workflow_ops.py and
config.py against ONE shared bound. Tightening it for config.py would also have tightened it for
workflow_ops.py — still 794 until b5fe lands — so the test would have gone red naming the WRONG
ticket's file. Split into a per-file table: config.py at the 700 policy target, workflow_ops.py left
at the staged cap. b5fe changes one number when it lands.

HONEST LIMIT, stated in the new module's docstring as the plan requires: this RELOCATES INERT MASS
and does NOT remove the absorber. `from_env` still costs 10-13 lines per new knob, and the domain
moved out was chosen partly because it is inert (no growth since 2026-07-09). Roughly fifteen knobs
of runway, not permanence. The durable follow-ups are (a) teach gen_env_registry.py to consume an
exported spec list and only THEN table-ify from_env, or (b) domain-split the knobs per feature
cluster. ADR 0056's declarative-field-table suggestion remains NOT viable as written: the generator
records a read only when the env name is a STRING LITERAL, so a spec-row table makes 19 rows vanish
from docs/env-vars.md and fails the CI drift gate.

GATES: make lint clean (after rewrapping over-long docstring prose — ruff format does not reflow
docstrings), make typecheck clean, docs/env-vars.md regenerated for the moved
REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED row. A broad tests/unit + tests/interfaces run is in progress as independent
no-regression evidence.

NOT CLOSING until 1157 is Verified +1.

# Extract the gate read-root/session domain out of llm/config.py

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at 793 LOC against the absolute 800 cap, so SEVEN lines of headroom, and
it is the most CENTRAL near-cap file in the repo (fan-in 93). Ticket d23e's entire scope is this file
— a `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` deprecation alias, which must keep honouring the old name, warn, and prefer the
new. MEASURED comparable: the `REBAR_LLM_MAX_ITERS` tombstone (`3eb3e71337`) cost +8 lines, and an
alias is strictly bigger than a tombstone, so realistically 10-16 lines. Per-knob cost in this file is
MEASURED at 10-13 lines. d23e is genuinely blocked.

## Approach
**ADR 0056 §Decision 5 pre-diagnosed this file and its prescription does NOT hold. Do not follow it.**
It said config.py's problem is "178 lines of FLAT independent env reads" wanting "a declarative field
table". Verified against the tree:
 * The SPAN claim holds (`from_env` is `config.py:575-753` = 179 lines) but the characterisation does
   not. Only 125 of those lines are the flat `return cls(...)`; the other 53 are an ORDERING-COUPLED
   preamble (the tombstone raise at `:581-584` must precede everything; `table`/`cli` must precede
   every read; `current_code_root()` must beat the env var, `:617-625`). Of 29 kwargs, 22 are regular
   and SEVEN are irregular (a derived non-knob `runner`; `api_key` env-only by secret policy; a 3-way
   `repo_path` cascade rooted in a ContextVar; `tickets_path` with no env var at all; 20 lines of
   custom `mcp_servers` JSON parsing; a nested `LangfuseConfig`; an enum-validating `overlap_drain`),
   plus two field/env/file name mismatches a convention-driven table cannot derive.
 * **A TABLE WOULD BREAK THE ENV-VAR DRIFT GATE — this is the crux.** `scripts/gen_env_registry.py`
   is a pure AST walk with no name resolution: it recognises a read only when the name argument is a
   STRING LITERAL (`:117-124`) and files anything else under "dynamically-constructed reads", where
   the variable DISAPPEARS from the table. A loop over spec rows makes that argument an
   `ast.Attribute`, so all 19 currently-resolved rows vanish from `docs/env-vars.md` and CI fails.
   `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py:259-267` exists to catch this class and names the precedent
   ("exactly what happened on sibling task f844"); `llm/model_classes.py:112-130` spells out nine
   literal `os.environ.get` calls rather than one indirection for the same reason. **The repo has
   already tried the table shape here and rejected it.**
 * In-file, a table nets roughly ZERO lines anyway (~66 lines of rows replacing ~110, plus ~20 of
   dispatch). It relieves nothing.

**What the ADR missed, and what this ticket does instead: 219 of the 793 lines are not configuration
at all.** `config.py:51-152` and `:190-269` are the gate read-root / snapshot-session domain — four
ContextVars and eleven functions (`current_code_root`, `resolve_code_root`, `current_tickets_root`,
`current_code_sha`, `in_gate_session`, `gate_session`, `assert_gated`, `use_code_root`,
`use_tickets_root`). `assert_gated` (`:216-240`) raises about `rebar.llm.gate_source` — it is a
RUNTIME FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY GUARD, not a config knob.

Three properties make this the right cut rather than a mechanical carve:
 1. **The seam already has a consumer proving it real.** `llm/gate_source.py:35` imports exactly
    `gate_session, use_code_root, use_tickets_root`, and its module docstring (`:1-18`) already
    documents the block being moved.
 2. **The domain is INERT.** All 154 lines of gate-context growth landed in five commits on or before
    2026-07-09; ZERO since. Every commit after that date landed in the knob region. So this moves
    cold mass out of the way of the hot region.
 3. **One-way dependency, no cycle.** `gate_context` needs only stdlib + `rebar.config` + a lazy
    `rebar.llm.errors`; it imports NOTHING from `llm.config`. `llm.config` imports it at module scope
    for `from_env`. This respects `model_classes.py:16-20`'s rule that config must never import back.

LEAVE `config.py:155-187` (`_active_gate_config`, `gate_config`, `resolve_gate_config`) IN PLACE — it
is genuinely about `LLMConfig` and moving it buys a lazy import for no benefit.

**HONEST LIMIT, state it in the change and the ADR: this RELOCATES MASS, it does NOT REMOVE THE
ABSORBER.** The absorber is the ~10-13 line per-knob cost in `from_env`, and the only structural fix
for that is blocked by the scanner. This buys about 15 knobs of runway, not permanence. The durable
follow-ups are (a) teach `gen_env_registry.py` to consume an exported spec list — precedent exists at
`:150-160` where it already imports and unions `rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY` — and only THEN table-ify,
or (b) domain-split the knobs per feature cluster (the 12 `overlap_*` fields are ~115 lines but change
`cfg.overlap_k` to `cfg.overlap.k` at ~31 sites). Both are separate epics.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — remove `:51-152` and `:190-269`; add a re-export block.
- `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` — NEW, ~202 LOC (clears the 100-LOC floor).
- `docs/env-vars.md` — one regenerated cell: `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` moves file (`config.py:227`).
- `tests/unit/` — the headroom guard.

## Testing
**The relocation must require ZERO test edits. A required edit means the cut is wrong.**
THE RULE THAT MAKES THAT TRUE: re-export the moved names from `llm.config` and repoint NO consumer in
`src/`. 13 monkeypatch targets name a moved symbol, and every consumer of `current_code_sha` /
`assert_gated` uses a FUNCTION-LEVEL `from rebar.llm.config import ...` (verified at `attest.py:123`,
`:251`, `:429`, `sidecar.py:404`, `runner.py:259`), so the name is resolved in `config`'s globals at
call time — exactly what `monkeypatch.setattr` rebinds. Repointing a consumer while a test patches
`rebar.llm.config.<name>` is the silent-break mode ADR 0056 warns about.

Loud canaries, which fail at COLLECTION if the re-export is wrong:
`tests/interfaces/store/test_pass1_fanout_gate_session.py:19` and
`tests/unit/test_code_review_gate_session.py:27` both do a module-scope
`from rebar.llm.config import <moved name>`. `tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:173` patches
`llm_config.assert_gated` and fails loudly if the rebind stops taking effect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at or below 640 LOC and `src/rebar/llm/gate_context.py` is at least
      100 and under 800
- [ ] the seam guard for `llm/config.py` is TIGHTENED from the staged `<= 800` that sibling d8ef
      introduces to the `< 700` policy target, in this same change — the change that creates the
      headroom is the one that may assert it. (d8ef ships the staged bound because config.py is 793
      today; do not re-add a guard, tighten the existing one in
      `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py`.)
- [ ] the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file
- [ ] no module under `src/` imports the moved names from `gate_context` — every consumer still reaches
      them through `rebar.llm.config`, so the monkeypatch targets keep working
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_env_registry.py` leaves the tree clean, with the moved
      `REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED` row regenerated rather than hand-edited
- [ ] the NEW module's docstring states, IN-REPO, that this relocates inert mass and does NOT remove
      the per-knob absorber in `from_env` — so the next reader sizing up config.py's growth curve
      meets that caveat in the code rather than in a ticket they will not read
- [ ] `assert_gated`'s hardcoded `logging.getLogger("rebar.llm.config")` (`config.py:230`) is
      re-pointed to the module that actually contains it after the move, and a test asserts the
      REBAR_GATE_ALLOW_UNGATED override warning is emitted on the `gate_context` logger rather than
      the `config` one. This is an AUDITED security-relevant warning — the message itself says the
      override is "audited" — so attributing it to a module that no longer holds the code sends
      whoever greps the logs to the wrong file. VERIFIED SAFE to change: `grep -rn '"rebar.llm.config"'
      src/ tests/` returns ONLY that one line, so no test filters on the name and no consumer keys
      off it. Swept the rest of the moved block for the same class: the only other identity literals
      are the three `ContextVar` debug names, which remain accurate under `rebar.llm` and need no
      change

- [ ] [operator-attested] the same caveat appears in the Gerrit commit message. Tagged because the
      completion verifier reads repository files ONLY and cannot read git history, so a criterion
      about a commit message is unconfirmable from the codebase and would burn a close cycle
